html:
Welcome to RecoveryBot. This deck walks through everything the site does today, from signing up to the tools a group runs itself with. Move through it with Next / Previous or the arrow keys, and open each part on screen as you go.

Anyone can make a free account. There is no admin approval; people confirm their email instead.

How to use it

  1. Go to the sign-up page and enter your name, email and a password.

  2. Tick the “I’m not a robot” box (a small puzzle that solves itself) and agree to the Terms.

  3. Open the confirmation email and click the link within 3 days. Didn’t get it? Ask for a new one at /users/confirmation/new.

  4. Sign in. You land on your home page, /people.

Privacy first: no cookie banner (every cookie is needed and first-party), and the Privacy page lists exactly what is collected.

Follow along: Sign up · Resend confirmation · Sign in · Privacy · Terms

After signing in you land on /people. Two thirds is your Notes feed (yours plus what people you follow share). The other third shows your next meetings, sobriety birthdays and events from your groups.

How to use it

  1. Write a note at the top of the feed, or scroll to read.

  2. Use the side panel to see what is coming up in your groups.

  3. On a phone, the side panel folds under the feed.

Follow along: Your home feed

Your page lives at /people/your-username and is laid out in the HMBLBOT Editor. Account settings are at /users/edit.

How to use it

  1. Open Settings to change your name, username, email (a new address must be confirmed) and password.

  2. Choose who can see your new notes and highlights by default: Private, Followers or Members.

  3. Use Edit my page to arrange blocks: feed, about, groups, people, headings, photos and notes.

  4. You can delete your own account on the profile page with your password.

Follow along: My page · Edit my page · Account settings

Notes are short posts written in Markdown, with up to 6 pictures, on your timeline. You decide who sees each one.

How to use it

  1. Write a note and pick its visibility: Private, Followers or Members; share it with your groups if you want them to see it.

  2. Others who can see it can react (Like, Love, Hugs), comment, and repost notes shared with Members.

  3. Paste a link and a preview card appears. Remove it with the X if you don’t want it.

  4. Select text to bold, italicise, underline, strike through or add a link.

A repost never widens who can see a note: narrowing or deleting the original removes its reposts.

Follow along: Write a note

Follow people to see what they share. There is no approval step, and the person you follow gets a notification.

How to use it

  1. Open someone’s profile at /people/their-username.

  2. Press Follow. Their shared notes appear in your home feed.

  3. Unfollow any time from the same button.

Follow along: Find people from your feed

Recovery books are organised as Books, Chapters and Readings, and read in the browser.

How to use it

  1. Browse the library and open a book, then a chapter.

  2. Use the rich-text reader; admins edit chapters in the chapter editor.

  3. Groups pick which books they approve, so their members see their own shelf first.

Follow along: Open the library

Readings are pieces people write and share: a title, the text, and example topics for sharing.

How to use it

  1. Open My readings and press New reading.

  2. Write it in the editor, add example topics, and choose draft, scheduled or published.

  3. Share the link; link previews show the title and a card, never the full text, to chat apps.

Follow along: All readings · My readings · New reading

A random topic generator for group discussion, with sets of topics, a timer and a copy button.

How to use it

  1. Open /topicificator and choose a Topic Set in Settings.

  2. Press Shuffle for a random topic, the # button to pick by number, or Previous to go back.

  3. Use Free Share / Check-In when there is no topic, and the Copy button to paste the list into chat.

  4. Hosts can run it from a HostDeck: open the live window in Open to share, then draw topics and run the timer from the deck.

Follow along: Open the Topicificator

Everything that reaches the bell can also be pushed to your phone or computer.

How to use it

  1. Open /install and follow the steps for iPhone/iPad, Android or computer to add RecoveryBot to your home screen.

  2. In Settings, turn on Notifications on this device and send yourself a test.

  3. Tap a notification to open the right page; it is marked read.

On iPhone, adding it to the home screen is required for push notifications.

Follow along: Install steps · Notification settings

Find a meeting lists AA meetings from AA Intergroup and RecoveryBot’s own groups, in your time zone. No account needed.

How to use it

  1. Open /groups/meetings and search or filter.

  2. Open a listing to see details, the group’s page and how to join.

  3. Press Share for a card, link, or your phone’s share sheet.

Follow along: Find a meeting

A group has a public page, a members’ area and tools to run itself. Access is rolling out, so some accounts see Groups first.

How to use it

  1. Find your group and press Ask to join, or use an invite link.

  2. Wait for an admin to approve the request; you then see the members’ tabs.

  3. Group admins design the Home tab in the HMBLBOT Editor (Edit page) and manage members, roles and settings.

Follow along: Groups

Every weekly meeting has a host and a co-host place. The Hosts tab keeps the schedule and fills gaps.

How to use it

  1. Open the group’s Hosts tab.

  2. Schedulers assign names (and link them to accounts) for the whole series or one date.

  3. Anyone holding a place can press I can’t make it to ask for a sub; people marked can host are told and can take it.

  4. Turn on host reminders in Settings to be notified before your date.

Follow along: Your groups (open the Hosts tab)

HostDeck (the Hosting Command Center) is the one screen a host runs a meeting from: script, chat postings, readings, timer, service and milestones, shared live with the co-host.

How to use it

  1. Open Host and pick a meeting (or a date).

  2. Move through the script with Next / Previous; both hosts see where you are.

  3. Copy chat postings with one tap; the ones already posted are marked.

  4. Pick the day’s reading or activity: a chapter, today’s daily page, your own reading, Topicificator topics, a speaker or a meditation.

  5. Share the short link under Share with your co-host (/h/CODE); people without accounts see the chat postings.

  6. Host coordinators set up the script, postings and layout from the gear.

Follow along: Your groups (open Host)

A deck is HostDeck for anything a group runs from a document: a business meeting, host onboarding, an event day.

How to use it

  1. Open a document and choose to make a deck from it, or create one on the group’s HostDeck page.

  2. Lay it out in the layout editor: flow, notes, checklists, timers, share queue and more.

  3. In the deck’s gear, use Share this deck: copy the link, and choose whether people without an account can follow it read-only (with or without the script).

  4. Make a new link any time to retire the old one.

Follow along: Your groups (open HostDeck)

The group’s record-keeping area, at /groups/your-group/conscience, for members. Record keepers (marked by an admin) write; everyone in the group reads.

How to use it

  1. Documents: bylaws, formats and minutes in folders, each Public, Members, Hosts or Keepers only; edit in place, keep version history, import Word, RTF or PDF, and Save as PDF.

  2. Decisions: record motions, votes and who moved them, link what replaces what, and see the standing decisions. Robert’s Rules guidance flags missing seconds or counts that don’t carry.

  3. Business meetings: plan a meeting, build its agenda (members suggest items), record minutes, post them for the group; unfinished business carries over.

  4. Elected officials: positions, terms and reminders when a term is nearly up.

  5. Treasury: monthly treasurer’s reports with the prudent reserve and splits.

  6. Court verifications: a group’s own form at /court_verifications/new?group=your-group.

That is the tour. Thank you for being here.

Follow along: Your groups (open Conscience) · Court verification form · Questions? Contact us
